title: Reject the decorative bento grid
intent: Keep the grid only when the content is truly heterogeneous, because otherwise the page has no argument left to make with layout.
when_to_use: the cells hold different kinds of content with different natural shapes: a chart, a quote, a captured screen, a spec list
the grid is the argument, as in an evidence wall for a case study
when_not_to_use: the cell count does not equal the content count, so a cell is empty or the last row is short
all cells hold the same kind of content, which makes it a card row with irregular gaps
the grid exists to make a thin page look designed
rules: cell count equals content count exactly, with no filler cell and no empty cell
no two adjacent cells share the same aspect ratio
every cell's span is justified by its content type in the layout plan, not chosen for visual balance
if replacing the grid with equal cells loses nothing but rhythm, the layout is rejected and a ranked stack or a table is used instead
trade_off: You hand back an easy way to look busy. A heterogeneous grid is harder to fill, and any cell you cannot fill with a different content type has to be cut from the page.
failure_mode: The grid is filled with decoration: oversized numerals, icon tiles, and a colour block carrying a slogan, so the section is a mosaic of nothing and the empty cells multiply.

example.brief: Dashboard product page holding five unrelated claims.
example.ruling: Bento is rejected. Two claims are cut, one becomes a wide chart panel with its source, one becomes a quote with attribution, and the rest fold into a written list. Four cells, four kinds of content.
